translationRepairs: Such are the triple steps, nine columns, twenty-seven senior officials, eighty-one junior gentlemen, the Dipper, the crossbar, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Jupiter’s “grasping” lodges, and their kind.

Such are the triple steps, nine columns, twenty-seven senior officials, eighty-one junior gentlemen, the Dipper, the crossbar, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the Sheti (“Grasping”) asterism, and their kind.
摄提 is the Sheti asterism, flanking Dajiao near the Dipper handle; it is not 'Jupiter's lodges'.

When Han rose, in the reigns of Jing and Wu, Sima Tan and his son Qian—descendants by marriage of the Li clan—held the post of Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records and composed the Treatise on Celestial Offices.

When Han rose, in the reigns of Jing and Wu, Sima Tan and his son Qian—hereditary descendants of the Li clan—held the post of Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records and composed the Treatise on Celestial Offices.
以世黎氏之后 means 'as hereditary descendants of the Li clan' (世 'generation after generation'); nothing indicates descent by marriage.

When Han arose, in the time of Jing and Wu, there were Sima Tan and Tan's son Qian; as descendants by marriage of the Li clan, they served as Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records of the Grand Historian and composed the Treatise on the Celestial Offices.

When Han arose, in the time of Jing and Wu, there were Sima Tan and Tan's son Qian; as hereditary descendants of the Li clan, they served as Grand Astrologer; Qian wrote the Records of the Grand Historian and composed the Treatise on the Celestial Offices.
以世黎氏之后 means 'as hereditary descendants of the Li clan' (世 'generation after generation'); nothing indicates descent by marriage.
Later there was a man named Feng.
Later there were those who drew upon it.
馮 here is the verb 'rely on / draw upon' (憑), not a person named Feng; the sentence introduces the moon myth.
Later there was one named Feng.
Later there were those who relied upon it.
馮 here is the verb 'rely on / draw upon' (憑), not a person named Feng; the sentence introduces the moon myth.
Before she went, she had Mei divined with You Huang, who read the omen: 'Auspicious.
Before she went, she had You Huang divine for her with stalks, and he read the omen: 'Auspicious.
枚筮 means divination by counting stalks; 'Mei' is not a name.
About to go, she had Mei divined by You Huang; You Huang divined and said: 'Auspicious.
About to go, she had it divined with stalks by You Huang; You Huang divined and said: 'Auspicious.
枚筮 means divination by counting stalks; 'Mei' is not a name.

Next year’s first month saw Guangwu rise at Chunling while Xinshi and Lower Yang rebels under Zhang Ang and Wang Chang joined Gengshi’s host; together they broke Nanyang, cut down Mang’s minister Zhen Fu and Liangqiu Ci, and slaughtered tens of thousands.

Next year’s first month saw Guangwu rise at Chunling while Xinshi and Xiajiang (Lower River) rebels under Zhang Ang and Wang Chang joined Gengshi’s host; together they broke Nanyang, cut down Mang’s minister Zhen Fu and Liangqiu Ci, and slaughtered tens of thousands.
下江 is Xiajiang, the 'Lower River' rebel band, not 'Lower Yang'.
Tenth month, day wushen: Han troops poured in through Xuanyping Gate.
Tenth month, day wushen: Han troops poured in through Xuanping Gate.
宣平城門 is the Xuanping Gate; 'Xuanyping' is a misspelling.
Empress Guo was already estranged; soon she became dowager of Zhongshan as Honored Lady Yin ascended the throne.
Empress Guo was already estranged; soon she became dowager of Zhongshan as Honored Lady Yin was installed as empress.
陰貴人立為皇后 means Lady Yin was made empress; she did not ascend the throne.
Empress Guo had faded; in year seventeen’s tenth month she became Zhongshan dowager while Lady Yin ascended—the “palace cleared” omen.
Empress Guo had faded; in year seventeen’s tenth month she became Zhongshan dowager while Lady Yin was made empress—the “palace cleared” omen.
立陰貴人為皇后: Lady Yin was made empress; 'ascended' alone implies the throne.
The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; the handle of the Northern Dipper presides over executions.
The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; the bowl (kui) of the Northern Dipper presides over executions.
北斗魁 is the bowl (kui) of the Dipper, not its handle (杓).
A star coming out of the Supreme Palace Enclosure and striking the Dipper’s handle means a great imperial envoy will go forth to inflict punishment and death.
A star coming out of the Supreme Palace Enclosure and striking the Dipper’s bowl (kui) means a great imperial envoy will go forth to inflict punishment and death.
北斗魁 is the bowl (kui) of the Dipper, not its handle (杓).
Guangwu then told Wu Han to raise thirty thousand Nanyang troops, row upstream, and attack Gongsun Shu at White Emperor.
Guangwu then told Wu Han to raise thirty thousand Nanyang troops, row upstream, and attack Gongsun Shu, the self-styled White Emperor of Shu.
蜀白帝公孫述: 'White Emperor of Shu' is Gongsun Shu's self-styled title in apposition, not a place he was attacked at.
At that time Emperor Guangwu ordered Grand Marshal Wu Han to levy thirty thousand men from Nanyang, sail boats up the Yangzi, and strike Shu’s lord Gongsun Shu at Baidi.
At that time Emperor Guangwu ordered Grand Marshal Wu Han to levy thirty thousand men from Nanyang, sail boats up the Yangzi, and strike Gongsun Shu, the White Emperor of Shu.
蜀白帝公孫述: 'White Emperor of Shu' is Gongsun Shu's self-styled title in apposition, not a place he was attacked at.
Twelfth year, tenth month: Han pushed against Shu’s captain Yong, reached Guangdu, and killed Shi Xing.
Twelfth year, tenth month: Han pushed against Shu’s younger cousin Yong, Commandant of the Guards, reached Guangdu, and killed Shi Xing.
述从弟卫尉永: Yong was Gongsun Shu's younger cousin and Commandant of the Guards, not merely a 'captain'.
Feng Jun Who Inspires Awe seized Jiangzhou and cut down Tian Rong.
Feng Jun, General Who Awes the Caitiffs, seized Jiangzhou and cut down Tian Rong.
威虏將軍 is the title General Who Awes the Caitiffs; the idiomatic line garbles it into Feng Jun's name.
Zang Gong stormed Fuling and slew Shu’s brother, Grand Minister of Works Hui.
Zang Gong stormed Fu and slew Shu’s brother, Grand Minister of Works Hui.
涪 is Fu (Fu county/city), not Fuling (涪陵), a different place.
Zang Gong broke Fuling and killed Shu’s younger brother, grand minister of works Hui.
Zang Gong broke Fu and killed Shu’s younger brother, grand minister of works Hui.
涪 is Fu (Fu county/city), not Fuling (涪陵), a different place.
Next day Han sacked Chengdu, executed Huang, Yan Cen, and other captains, killed tens of thousands, and wiped out over ten thousand of the consort clan.
Next day Han sacked Chengdu, executed Gongsun Huang, Yan Cen, and other captains, killed tens of thousands, and wiped out over ten thousand of Gongsun Shu's wife's clan.
公孫晃 is Gongsun Huang; 述妻宗族 is Gongsun Shu's wife's clan, not a 'consort clan'.
A stray fire also threaded the Northern Dipper for 113 days, dying northeast of the Ghosts.

A guest star with a two-foot flame also appeared among the Seven Stars lodge and moved southwest; on the twenty-second day of the next year’s second month it vanished six feet northeast of the Ghosts, after 113 days.
七星 is the Seven Stars lunar lodge (Xing), not the Northern Dipper, and 客星 is a guest star; the idiomatic line also drops the direction, flame length and vanishing date.
The Seven Stars lodge’s field is Zhou.
七星 here is the Seven Stars lodge, whose field-allocation is Zhou; it is not the Dipper.
The bracketed character 鏚 (a kind of axe) is read qi, not qiang.
The bracketed character 鏚 (a kind of axe) is read qi, not qiang.
